title: Period-equality conjecture for nim-sequences and zero-position sequences
source_name: Nhan Bao Ho, “On the expansion of three-element subtraction sets”, arXiv:1202.2986 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1202.2986

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2012).
statement:
Let $G$ be a subtraction game, let $\mathcal{G}(n)$ denote the nim-value of a pile of size $n$, and define the zero-position indicator sequence $\mathcal{V}(n)$ by

$$
\mathcal{V}(n)=
\begin{cases}
0,&\text{if }\mathcal{G}(n)=0;\\
1,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
$$

**Period-equality conjecture.** For every subtraction game, the sequences $\{\mathcal{G}(n)\}$ and $\{\mathcal{V}(n)\}$ have the same period $p$. Since subtraction-game nim-sequences are periodic, the indicator sequence is periodic as well; the conjecture asserts that passing to zero versus nonzero nim-values does not reduce the period. Its general status is open.

title: Period conjecture for three-parameter Subtraction Nim
source_name: Yuto Moriwaki, “Subtraction Nim with Continuous Parameters”, arXiv:2606.11658 (2026).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2312.02426](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.02426).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.11658

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).
statement:
Let $G(S)$ be the normal-play Subtraction Nim game with move set $S=\{a,b,c\}$, where $0<a<b<c$ and $c\ne a+b$. Its Nim value function is considered as a function of the heap or string length.

**Period conjecture.** The Nim value function is periodic with a period equal to one of $a+b$, $b+c$, or $c+a$.

This is the same period claim attributed earlier in the paper to Ward, so it is merged with that conjecture. The supplied text gives no proof or resolution in general.

title: The inheritance of no discrepancy for dominant three-action subtraction sets
source_name: Anjali Bhagat, Tanmay Kulkarni, Urban Larsson and Divya Murali, “Tie-breaking in self interest cumulative subtraction games”, arXiv:2510.24280 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.24280

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).
statement:
Let $S=\{s_3,s_2,s_1\}$ with $s_3<s_2<s_1$, and let a friendly/antagonistic discrepancy mean a difference between the FvF and AvA self-interest games. **Dominant three-action inheritance conjecture.** If

$$
s_1\geq 2s_2
$$

and the two-action set $\{s_3,s_2\}$ has no discrepancy for any heap size $x$, then $S$ has no friendly/antagonistic discrepancy for any heap size $x$. The claim is an empirical conjecture about extending the two-action pattern to three actions; no proof or resolution is supplied.

title: Twin-period recurrence conjecture for reversible elementary cellular automaton 115
source_name: Enrico Formenti and Supreeti Kamylia, “The Curious Case of Reversible Elementary Second Order Cellular Automaton 115”, arXiv:2606.13159 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13159

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).
statement:
Let reversible elementary second-order cellular automaton 115 (RESOCA 115) have finite configurations with periods. Two periods $p$ and $p+3$ are called **twins**. 

**Twin-period recurrence conjecture.** Assume that $p$ and $p+3$ are twin periods. Then the next twin pair is $p'$ and $p'+3$, where

$$
p'=2p+\frac{9-3(-1)^p}{2}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a recurrence for the experimentally observed twin periods of finite configurations of RESOCA 115; the source states that the authors do not know whether all periods are twins and presents the recurrence as a pattern suggested by experiments.

title: Odd-index period formula conjecture for the family $1(01)^k$
source_name: Enrico Formenti and Supreeti Kamylia, “The Curious Case of Reversible Elementary Second Order Cellular Automaton 115”, arXiv:2606.13159 (2026).
references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2606.02792](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.02792), [arXiv:2101.09027](https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.09027), [arXiv:0910.1258](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1258).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13159

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).
statement:
Consider the family of finite configurations whose current binary word is $1(01)^k$, with period function $P(k)$ assigning to the configuration indexed by $k$ its period. 

**Odd-index period formula conjecture.** The period function satisfies

$$
P(2i+1)=4^{2i+3}-1
$$

for $i\in\mathbb{N}$.
The formula is suggested by computational experiments, and the source explicitly says that it is suspected to hold for every $i\in\mathbb{N}$; no proof or resolution is given.

title: Even-index period formula conjecture for the family $1(01)^k$
source_name: Enrico Formenti and Supreeti Kamylia, “The Curious Case of Reversible Elementary Second Order Cellular Automaton 115”, arXiv:2606.13159 (2026).
references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2009–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2102.06956](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.06956), [arXiv:2008.01480](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01480), [arXiv:0910.1258](https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.1258).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.13159

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).
statement:
Consider the family of finite configurations whose current binary word is $1(01)^k$, with period function $P(k)$ assigning to the configuration indexed by $k$ its period. 

**Even-index period formula conjecture.** The period function satisfies

$$
P(2i)=\frac{2\cdot4^{2i+2}-7\cdot4^{i+1}+5}{3}
$$

for $i\in\mathbb{N}$.
This formula is inferred from experimentally observed base-$4$ patterns for the periods at even indices; the source presents it as a conjectural formula and gives no proof or resolution.

title: Cyclotomic Catalan triangle conjecture
source_name: Youssouf Wirdane, “Combinatorial study of the q-Catalan triangle and its generalizations”, arXiv:2605.14682 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14682

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).
statement:
For a positive integer $\mu$, let $\omega=e^{2i\pi/\mu}$ and define the cyclotomic analogue by

$$
C_{n,k}^{(\mu)}=C_{n,k}(\omega,\ldots,\omega).
$$

Assume that $\mu$ divides $n+1$.

**Cyclotomic Catalan conjecture.**

$$
C_{n,n}^{(\mu)}=\frac{1}{\mu}\binom{n+1}{(n+1)/\mu}.
$$

These specializations are presented as cyclotomic analogues related to the cyclic sieving phenomenon. The excerpt provides no proof or resolution status.

title: The parking-function formula for the second tree inversion enumerator
source_name: Sam Hopkins, “Two t-analogues of the tree inversion enumerator”, arXiv:2510.22385 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.22385

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2025).
statement:
Let $I_n(q,t)$ and $\widetilde{I}_n(q,t)$ be the two $t$-analogues of the tree inversion enumerator, let $\mathrm{PF}(n)$ denote the set of parking functions of length $n$, and for $\pi\in\mathrm{PF}(n)$ let $\mathrm{oc}(\pi)$ be its parking outcome permutation. Write $\mathrm{cosum}(a)$ for the cosum statistic and $\mathrm{des}(\sigma)$ for the number of descents of a permutation $\sigma$. **Parking-function formula.** Computational evidence suggests that

$$
\widetilde{I}_n(q,t) = \sum_{\pi \in \mathrm{PF}(n)}q^{\mathrm{cosum}(a)}t^{\mathrm{des}(\mathrm{oc}(\pi))}.
$$

The analogous formula for $I_n(q,t)$ is known from Stanley and Yin, whereas no such generating-function interpretation was previously available for $\widetilde{I}_n(q,t)$.

title: Xin's second determinant factorization conjecture
source_name: Christian Krattenthaler, “Advanced Determinant Calculus: A Complement”, arXiv:math/0503507 (2005).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0503507

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2005).
statement:
Let $cmu$ be an indeterminate, let $n$ be an odd non-negative integer, and use $cdelta_{ij}$ and shifted factorial notation as in the first conjecture.

**Xin's second determinant conjecture.**

$$
cdet_{0cle i,jcle n-1}cleft(-cdelta_{ij}+cbinom{cmu+i+j}{j+2}cright)
$$

is equal to the product displayed in the source statement.

The claim concerns the next determinant in the same family; the source says that the factorization occurs for odd $n$ but not for even $n$. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

title: Xin–Zhang's tridiagonal determinant conjecture
source_name: Jiaqiang Hu and Chen Zhang, “A proof of Xin-Zhang's tridiagonal determinant conjecture (extended version)”, arXiv:2601.03082 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.03082

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2026); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)
statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $t$ be a parameter, and let $C$ be the $(n-1)\times(n-1)$ matrix with entries

$$
C_{i,j}=\begin{cases} t-(n-2i+2)(n-1-i)-1,&\text{if }i=j;\\ (i-1)(n-i),&\text{if }i=j+1;\\ -(n-1-i)(n-i),&\text{if }i=j-1;\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}
$$

**Xin–Zhang's determinant conjecture.** The determinant of $C$ is

$$
\det C=\begin{cases}(t-n+1)\displaystyle\prod_{i=0}^{r-2}\bigl(t-n+1-r(r-1)+i(i+1)\bigr)^2,&\text{if }n=2r;\\ (t-n+1)\bigl(t-n+1-(r-1)^2\bigr)\displaystyle\prod_{i=1}^{r-2}\bigl(t-n+1-(r-1)^2+i^2\bigr)^2,&\text{if }n=2r-1.\end{cases}
$$

This product formula gives the characteristic polynomial associated with a recurrence enumerating nonnegative integer matrices with equal row and column sums, and is related to the Ehrhart polynomial of the Birkhoff polytope. The paper proves the conjecture by showing that a scalar shift of $C$ is similar to a lower triangular matrix, so its characteristic polynomial factors through the diagonal entries.

title: The symmetry conjecture for the array $M$
source_name: Guoce Xin and Yueming Zhong, “Proving some conjectures on Kekulé numbers for certain benzenoids by using Chebyshev polynomials”, arXiv:2201.02376 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.02376

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).
statement:
Let $M=(M_{n,k})_{n,k\geq 0}$ be the array associated with the row numerators $H_n(x)$ of the generating functions of $T(n,m)$.

**Symmetry conjecture for $M$.** For all nonnegative integers $n$ and $k$,

$$
M_{n,k}=M_{k,n}.
$$

Equivalently, the array $M$ is symmetric about its main diagonal; the displayed central terms begin $1,3,31,623,\ldots$.

This conjecture concerns the symmetry of the array encoding the coefficients of the row numerators. It is stated as one of the conjectures associated with OEIS sequence A205497; the supplied material gives no resolution status.

title: Pascal recurrence conjecture for generalized Pascal triangles
source_name: Michael A. Allen and Kenneth Edwards, “On Two Families of Generalizations of Pascal's Triangle”, arXiv:2201.13253 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.13253

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).
statement:
Let $m,n,k$ be integers, and let $\left\langle\begin{matrix}n\\#2\end{matrix}\right\rangle_m$ denote the $(n,k)$-th entry of the generalized Pascal triangle of parameter $m$. For $k\geq 0$, consider entries satisfying

$$
n\geq (m-1)k+1.
$$

**Pascal recurrence conjecture.** For $n\geq (m-1)k+1$ when $k\geq 0$,

$$
\left\langle\begin{matrix}n\\#2\end{matrix}\right\rangle_m=\left\langle\begin{matrix}n-1\\#2\end{matrix}\right\rangle_m+\left\langle\begin{matrix}n-1\\#2\end{matrix}\right\rangle_m.
$$

This generalizes the Pascal recurrence, and the source states that it has been verified for $m=1,2,3$; its validity for general $m$ remains open.

title: Semicompleteness of the hypercube division sequences
source_name: Zachary Hoelscher, “Semicomplete Arithmetic Sequences, Division of Hypercubes, and the Pell Constant”, arXiv:2102.07083 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.07083

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).
statement: Let $C_M^N$ denote the maximum number of pieces into which an $M$-dimensional hypercube can be cut using $N-1$ hyperplanes, and let $\{C_M^N\}$ be the resulting sequence as $N$ varies. A sequence of positive, strictly increasing integers is **semicomplete** if, for every $j>2$ and every natural number $k<\lfloor G\rfloor$, the integer $k$ can be represented as a sum of distinct terms from the first $j$ sequence terms divided by $j$, where $G$ is the sum of those $j$ fractions. **The hypercube division conjecture.** The sequence $\{C_M^N\}$ is semicomplete for every natural number $M\geq 1$. This would establish semicompleteness for an infinite family of sequences; the cases $M=1,2,3,4$ are proved in the paper, while the general case remains open.

title: Polynomial formulas for truncated total depth in ordered trees
source_name: Stoyan Dimitrov, Martin Minchev and Yan Zhuang, “BFS versus DFS for fixed-level targets in ordered trees”, arXiv:2404.05664 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.05664

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).
statement:
Let $n$ and $\ell$ be integers satisfying $n\geq \ell\geq 1$. Let $\operatorname{totalD}(n,k)$ denote the total quantity studied in the paper, and let $\operatorname{totalDTrunc}(n,k)$ denote its truncated version. For each $\ell$, let $a_{\ell}(n)$ and $b_{\ell}(n)$ be polynomials in $n$. **Polynomial-formula conjecture.** For all $n\geq \ell\geq 1$, \

$$
\operatorname{totalD}(n,2\ell-1)-\operatorname{totalDTrunc}(n,2\ell-1)=\frac{a_{\ell}(n)}{(n+2\ell+2)^{(2\ell-2)}}{2n \choose n-2\ell-1}
\
$$

 and \

$$
\operatorname{totalD}(n,2\ell)-\operatorname{totalDTrunc}(n,2\ell)=\frac{b_{\ell}(n)}{(n+2\ell+4)^{(2\ell-2)}}{2n+1 \choose n-2\ell-2}.
\
$$

 Here $a_{\ell}(n)$ and $b_{\ell}(n)$ have degree $2\ell-2$ and non-negative integer coefficients; the leading coefficient of $a_{\ell}(n)$ is $2\ell-1$, and the leading coefficient of $b_{\ell}(n)$ is $\ell$. The conjecture would provide a simplified expression for $\operatorname{totalDTrunc}(n,\ell)$, but the supplied text gives no resolution.

title: Reiner–Stanton conjecture on unimodality of symmetric q-binomial differences
source_name: Richard P. Stanley and Fabrizio Zanello, “A generalization of a 1998 unimodality conjecture of Reiner and Stanton”, arXiv:1711.10033 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.10033

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2017). “That conjecture is also open in general.”
statement:
Let $k$, $m$, and $b$ be integers with $k\ge 2$, $m\ge k$, and, for $k\ge 3$, $k-2\le b\le \frac{km-4k+4}{k-2}$, where $k(m-b)$ is even. Define

$$
f(k,m,b)(q)=\binom{m}{k}_q-q^{\frac{k(m-b)}{2}+b-2k+2}\binom{b}{k-2}_q.
$$

Here $\binom{m}{k}_q$ denotes the $q$-binomial coefficient. **Reiner–Stanton conjecture.** The polynomial $f(k,m,b)(q)$ is nonnegative and unimodal for all $m\gg_k0$ and all $b\le \frac{km-4k+4}{k-2}$ satisfying $kb\equiv km\pmod 2$, with the only exception of $b=\frac{km-4k+2}{k-2}$ when this is an integer.

The conjecture generalizes the original Reiner–Stanton prediction about symmetric differences of $q$-binomial coefficients. The paper proves the case $k=5$ and completely characterizes nonnegativity and unimodality for $k\le 5$; it also notes an isolated counterexample to the original conjecture when $k=3$. The cases $k\ge 6$ remain open in general.

title: Strict unimodality conjecture for Reiner–Stanton polynomials
source_name: William Y. C. Chen and Ivy D. D. Jia, “Semi-invariants of Binary Forms Pertaining to a Unimodality Theorem of Reiner and Stanton”, arXiv:2011.01467 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.01467

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2020).
statement:
Let

$$
F_{n,k}(q)={n+k\brack k}-q^{n}{n+k-2\brack k-2},
$$

where $k\geq 2$ and $n$ is even. A polynomial is **strictly unimodal, except for the two terms at both ends** when its coefficients strictly increase to the middle, apart from the two end terms. **Strict unimodality conjecture.** For $n\geq 8$ and $k\geq 15$, $F_{n,k}(q)$ is strictly unimodal, except for the two terms at both ends. The conjecture is supported by numerical evidence, while the text does not report a proof or disproof.

title: Strict unimodality conjecture for the V-statistics
source_name: Nian Hong Zhou, “Unimodality and certain bivariate formal Laurent series”, arXiv:2408.04433 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.04433

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).
statement:
Let $V(m,n)$ and $V_d(m,n)$ be the coefficients of the bivariate formal series $\mathcal{V}(z,q)$ and $\mathcal{V}_d(z,q)$, respectively, and let $\mathscr{U}_{z,q}^1$ denote the paper's one-variable coefficientwise unimodality class. **Strict unimodality conjecture for the V-statistics.** Both series satisfy

$$
\mathcal{V}(z,q),\mathcal{V}_d(z,q)\in\mathscr{U}_{z,q}^1.
$$
 Equivalently, for all integers $m,n\ge 0$,

$$
V(m,n)\ge V(m+1,n)\qquad\text{and}\qquad V_d(m,n)\ge V_d(m+1,n).
$$
 The claim is supported by numerical verification for $n\le 50$; the paper presents it as a stronger conjecture concerning these two series.

title: Bergeron–Ceballos–Küstner's unimodality conjecture for q-Fibonomial coefficients
source_name: Brendan B. Connelly, Ezekiel Ito, Thomas C. Martinez, Olha Shevchenko and Kacey Yang, “Unimodality of q-Fibonomial coefficients for small cases”, arXiv:2605.12822 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12822

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2026).
statement:
For $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$, define the $q$-Fibonomial coefficient by

$$
\left[\\!\begin{matrix} m+n \\\\ n \end{matrix}\\!\right]_{\mathcal{F}}:=\frac{[F_{m+n}]^!_q}{[F_m]^!_q\\,[F_n]^!_q},
$$

where $[F_n]^!_q:=\prod_{k=1}^n[F_k]_q$ and $[n]_q:=1+q+\dots+q^{n-1}$. **Bergeron–Ceballos–Küstner's conjecture.** The polynomials

$$
\left[\\!\begin{matrix}m+n\\\
\end{matrix}\\!\right]_{\mathcal{F}}
$$

are unimodal. Bergeron–Ceballos–Küstner introduced these polynomials and conjectured unimodality, while the source proves the conjecture for $n\leq 3$; the general case remains open.

title: The $q$-rious unimodality conjecture
source_name: S. Ole Warnaar and Wadim Zudilin, “q-rious unimodality”, arXiv:2502.03993 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.03993

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2025).
statement:
Let $(\boldsymbol{a},\boldsymbol{b})$ be tuples of positive integers satisfying Landau's criterion, namely

$$
\sum_i\lfloor a_i x\rfloor-\sum_j\lfloor b_j x\rfloor\geqslant 0 \quad\text{for all }x\geqslant 0.
$$

Let $D(\boldsymbol{a},\boldsymbol{b};q)$ be the corresponding $q$-factorial quotient, and write its coefficients as $D(\boldsymbol{a},\boldsymbol{b};q)=\sum_{i=0}^k c_iq^i$. **$q$-rious unimodality conjecture.** The polynomial

$$
(1+q)D(\boldsymbol{a},\boldsymbol{b};q)
$$

is unimodal. This is proposed as a stronger statement implying the $q$-rious positivity conjecture, in a setting where the coefficient sequence of $D(\boldsymbol{a},\boldsymbol{b};q)$ is symmetric.

title: Unimodality conjecture for the two-variable Shi distance enumerator
source_name: Sivaramakrishnan Sivasubramanian, “Interpreting the two variable Distance enumerator of the Shi hyperplane arrangement”, arXiv:math/0610780 (2006).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0610780

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2006).
statement:
Let $\mathsf{Dist}_n(k,\ell)$ denote the number of regions of the Shi hyperplane arrangement having the statistics indexed by $k$ and $\ell$. For fixed $n$ and $k$, consider the sequence obtained by varying $\ell$.

**Unimodality conjecture.** For fixed $n,k$, the numbers $\mathsf{Dist}_n(k,\ell)$ as $\ell$ increases are unimodal.

This conjecture concerns the coefficient distribution of the two-variable refinement of the Shi arrangement's distance enumerator. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture is known or resolved.

title: Morier-Genoud–Ovsienko unimodality conjecture for fence rank sequences
source_name: Sergi Elizalde and Bruce Sagan, “Partial rank symmetry of distributive lattices for fences”, arXiv:2201.03044 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.03044

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of January 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)
statement: Let $F(\beta)$ be a fence and let $L(\beta)$ be the distributive lattice of lower order ideals of $F(\beta)$. Its rank sequence is $r(\beta):r_0,r_1,\ldots,r_n$, where $r_k$ is the number of elements of $L(\beta)$ at rank $k$. **Morier-Genoud–Ovsienko's unimodality conjecture.** For all $\beta$, the sequence $r(\beta)$ is unimodal. This conjecture was stated by Morier-Genoud and Ovsienko and is described in the source as having since been proved.

title: Unimodality conjecture for rank polynomials of circular fence posets
source_name: Ezgi Kantarcı Oğuz, Cem Yalım Özel and Mohan Ravichandran, “Chainlink Polytopes and Ehrhart-Equivalence”, arXiv:2211.08382 (2022).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2112.00518](https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.00518).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.08382

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2022).
statement:
Let $\bar{a}$ be a tuple of positive integers, and let $\overline{F}(\bar{a})$ be the corresponding circular fence poset with rank polynomial $\overline{R}(\bar{a};q)$. A polynomial is **unimodal** if its coefficients weakly increase up to a point and then weakly decrease. **Circular-fence rank-polynomial conjecture.** The rank polynomial $\overline{R}(\bar{a};q)$ of a circular fence poset $\overline{F}(\bar{a})$ is unimodal except when

$$
\bar{a}=(a,1,a,1)\quad\text{or}\quad(1,a,1,a)
$$

for some positive integer $a$. This conjecture concerns the apparent general unimodality of rank polynomials, with the displayed families as the proposed exceptions; the source reports that extensive computer calculations suggested it, but gives no resolution.

title: Conjecture on log-concavity and unimodality of involution statistics
source_name: W. M. B. Dukes, “Permutation statistics on involutions”, arXiv:math/0412222 (2004).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0412222

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2004).
statement:
For $n\geq 4$, let $\mathcal{I}_n^{\mathrm{maj}}(q)$ and $\mathcal{I}_n^{\mathrm{inv}}(q)$ denote the major-index and inversion generating polynomials over involutions, and let $Inv_n^B(q)$, $Inv_n^D(q)$, and $Inv_n^O(q)$ be the corresponding inversion polynomials for the types named in the source. For a polynomial $P(q)$, write $[q^i]P(q)$ for the coefficient of $q^i$.

**The conjecture.** For all $n\geq 4$:

1. The sequence $\{[q^i]\mathcal{I}_n^{\mathrm{maj}}(q)\}_{i=0}^{\binom{n}{2}}$ is log-concave.
2. For $2\leq i\leq \binom{n}{2}-2$,

$$
\bigl([q^i]\mathcal{I}_n^{\mathrm{inv}}(q)\bigr)^2\geq\bigl([q^{i-2}]\mathcal{I}_n^{\mathrm{inv}}(q)\bigr)\bigl([q^{i+2}]\mathcal{I}_n^{\mathrm{inv}}(q)\bigr).
$$

3. The sequences $\{[q^{2i}]Inv_n^B(q)\}_{i\geq0}$ and $\{[q^{2i+1}]Inv_n^B(q)\}_{i\geq0}$ are unimodal.
4. The sequences $\{[q^{2i}]Inv_n^D(q)\}_{i\geq0}$ and $\{[q^{2i+1}]Inv_n^D(q)\}_{i\geq0}$ are unimodal.
5. The sequences $\{[q^{2i}]Inv_n^O(q)\}_{i\geq0}$ and $\{[q^{2i+1}]Inv_n^O(q)\}_{i\geq0}$ are unimodal.

The conjecture extends the original log-concavity conjecture. The supplied passage reports numerical log-concavity through $n\leq14$ and notes that the relevant roots are not real and do not lie in the stated triangular region, but gives no resolution of these assertions.

title: Real-rootedness conjecture for the squares of the Eulerian and Delannoy triangles
source_name: Jianxi Mao and Lijie Wang, “The Narayana transformation”, arXiv:2607.01572 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01572

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2026). “Br\"and\'en and Jochemko studied the Eulerian transformation and disproved this conjecture.”
statement: Let $A$ and $D$ denote the Eulerian and Delannoy triangles, respectively, and let $A^2$ and $D^2$ be their matrix squares. For a lower triangular matrix $M$, write its $n$-th row generating function as $M_n(x)=\sum_k M(n,k)x^k$. **Real-rootedness conjecture.** The row generating functions of $A^2$ and $D^2$ have only real nonpositive roots. Numerical evidence supports this assertion for the row generating functions of $D^2$, while the conjecture concerns both triangles and remains open in the supplied text.

title: Sills–Zeilberger conjecture on the polynomials P_{01r}(N)
source_name: Cormac O'Sullivan, “On the partial fraction decomposition of the restricted partition generating function”, arXiv:1401.2809 (2014).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.2809

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2014).
statement:
For each integer $r\geqslant1$, define

$$
P_{01r}(N):=(-1)^N N!\,(-4)^r r!\,C_{01(N-r)}(N).
$$

**Sills–Zeilberger's conjecture.** For each $r\geqslant1$, $P_{01r}(N)$ is a monic, alternating, convex polynomial in $N$ of degree $2r$ whose only real roots are $0$ and $1$. The source records explicit examples and says that Sills and Zeilberger proved recursive top-down formulas for these polynomials, while this structural assertion remains conjectural.

title: D'Arcais polynomial positivity conjecture
source_name: Bernhard Heim und Markus Neuhauser, “Polynomization of Sun's Conjecture”, arXiv:2601.11226 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.11226

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2026). “The conjecture was proved by Wang and Zhu; shortly thereafter, Chen and Zheng independently obtained a second proof.”
statement:
Let $P_n^{\sigma}(x)$ denote the $n$th D'Arcais polynomial associated with the divisor-sum function $\sigma$, and define

$$
\Delta_n^{\sigma}(x):=(P_n^{\sigma}(x))^{n+1}-(P_{n+1}^{\sigma}(x))^n.
$$

**D'Arcais positivity conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 6$ and every real $x\geq 1$,

$$
(P_n^{\sigma}(x))^{n+1}-(P_{n+1}^{\sigma}(x))^n>0.
$$

At $x=1$, this specializes to Sun's conjecture for partition numbers. The supplied material does not state whether this broader polynomial claim has been resolved.

title: Merca's positivity conjecture for truncated Jacobi theta series
source_name: Nian Hong Zhou, “Positivity and tails of Jacobi theta series”, arXiv:2607.10968 (2026).
references: **10 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2606.27507](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.27507), [arXiv:2606.24243](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24243), [arXiv:2509.06357](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.06357), [arXiv:2411.13818](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.13818), [arXiv:2409.19907](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.19907), [arXiv:2408.09467](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.09467), [arXiv:2403.11608](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11608), [arXiv:2401.04019](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.04019), [arXiv:2005.03619](https://arxi
statement:
Let $R$ and $S$ be integers with $1\le S<R/2$, and let $k\ge1$. Consider the theta series

$$
\frac{(-1)^k}{(q^S;q^R)_\infty(q^{R-S};q^R)_\infty}\sum_{j\ge k}(-1)^jq^{j(j+1)R/2-jS}(1-q^{(2j+1)S}).
$$

**Merca's conjecture.** This theta series has non-negative coefficients. The conjecture refines the established positivity theorem for averaged truncations of Jacobi's triple product identity; its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.

title: A partition identity involving selected Ferrers-diagram points
source_name: Michel Lassalle, “A conjecture about partitions”, arXiv:math/9901040 (1999).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9901040

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 1999).
statement:
Let 
$$
be an indeterminate. A partition
$$
 has size $||$ and length $l$; write $m_i$ for the multiplicity of the part $i$, and set

$$
z_{}=_{i
e 1} i^{m_i}m_i!.
$$

For $r
e 0$, let 
$$
denote the number of ways to choose $r$ points in the Ferrers diagram of
$$
, with at least one selected point in every row. For an indeterminate $X$ and $n
e 0$, write $(a)_s=a(a+1)(a+s-1)$ and $\binom{X}{n}=[X]_n/n!$, where $[X]_n=X(X-1)(X-n+1)$.

**The partition identity conjecture.** For all integers $n,r,s
e 0$, the following equivalent identities hold:

$$
_{:||=n}(-1)^{r-l}^{l-1}_i_s=(s-1)!.
$$

$$

$$

Here the two forms are related by replacing $X$ with $-X$.

The conjecture generalizes classical binomial identities expressed as sums over partitions. It is trivial for $r>n$, and the authors verified it for $n\leq7$, for $s=1$, and for $r=1,2,3$; its general case remains open.

title: Odd-power symmetric sum conjecture
source_name: Petro Kolosov, “An unusual identity for odd-powers”, arXiv:2101.00227 (2021).
references:
**4 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1909.07269](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.07269), [arXiv:1712.08666](https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.08666), [arXiv:1504.05482](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.05482).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.00227

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).
statement:
Let $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $x$ be a positive integer. The coefficients ${\mathbf{A}}_{m,0}, {\mathbf{A}}_{m,1},\ldots,{\mathbf{A}}_{m,m}$ are constants independent of $x$ and $k$. **Odd-power symmetric sum conjecture.** For every $m\in\mathbb{N}$, there exist coefficients ${\mathbf{A}}_{m,0}, {\mathbf{A}}_{m,1},\ldots,{\mathbf{A}}_{m,m}$ such that

$$
x^{2m+1}=\sum_{k=1}^{x}\left({\mathbf{A}}_{m,0}k^0(x-k)^0+{\mathbf{A}}_{m,1}(x-k)^1+{\mathbf{A}}_{m,2}k^2(x-k)^2+\cdots+{\mathbf{A}}_{m,m}k^m(x-k)^m\right).
$$

The claim proposes a generalization of the displayed decomposition of $x^3$ as a sum of symmetric terms involving $k$ and $x-k$. The source does not provide a resolution or further conditions on the coefficients, so its status remains open.

title: GCD power-of-two conjecture for the coefficients of $c_m(c_1)$
source_name: A. V. Kitaev and A. Vartanian, “One-Parameter Meromorphic Solution of the Degenerate Third Painlevé Equation with Formal Monodromy Parameter a=i/2 Vanishing at the Origin”, arXiv:2305.17278 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.17278

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).
statement:
For $m\geqslant 2$, write the polynomial $c_m(c_1)$ as

$$
c_m(c_1)=\sum_{j=0}^{r_m}p_{m,j}c_1^j,
$$

where $r_m$ is defined by the paper's equation for the structure of $c_m(c_1)$. Let the greatest common divisor of its coefficients be

$$
\operatorname{g.c.d.}\,c_m(c_1):=\operatorname{g.c.d.}\{p_{m,0},p_{m,1},\ldots,p_{m,r_m}\}.
$$

Here $z_m\geqslant1$ is an integer sequence.

**GCD power-of-two conjecture.** For every $m\geqslant2$,

$$
\operatorname{g.c.d.}\,c_m(c_1)=2^{z_m}.
$$

The paper notes that divisibility by $2$ for all $m\geqslant2$ follows from the recurrence relation, while the asserted exact power-of-two form is suggested by computer calculations.

title: Finiteness conjecture for odd integers with equal binary digit sums 14 or 15
source_name: Karam Aloui, Damien Jamet, Hajime Kaneko, Steffen Kopecki, Pierre Popoli and Thomas Stoll, “On the binary digits of n and n^2”, arXiv:2203.05451 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.05451

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2022). “This conjecture remains still open.”
statement:
Let $s(n)$ denote the sum of the binary digits of $n$. For $k\in\{14,15\}$, consider odd integers $n$ satisfying

$$
s(n)=s(n^2)=k.
$$

**Finiteness conjecture.** Let $k\in\{14,15\}$. Then the number of odd integers $n$ with $s(n)=s(n^2)=k$ is finite.

The conjecture extends the paper's finite-case analysis for $k\in\{9,10,11\}$. A global search found no infinite family for $k=14$ or $k=15$ below $2^{80}$, but finiteness for these values remains open.

title: Marques–Trojovský conjecture on the Bonse inequality threshold function
source_name: Diego Marques and Pavel Trojovsky, “Asymptotic error terms in Bonse-type inequalities”, arXiv:2511.13691 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.13691

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).
statement:
Let $p_n$ denote the $n$-th prime, let $\pi(x)$ be the prime-counting function, and for $x\in\mathbb{R}$ define

$$
k(n,x)=n-\pi(n)+\frac{\pi(n)}{\pi(\log n)}-x\,\pi(\pi(n)).
$$

For $x\in\mathbb{R}$, let $\Psi(x)$ be the minimum, when it exists, of the integers $m\geq 8$ such that

$$
p_1p_2\cdots p_n>p_{n+1}^{k(n,x)}\quad\text{for all }n\geq m.
$$

**Marques–Trojovský conjecture.** The function $\Psi(x)$ satisfies: (i) $\Psi(x)=21$ for all $x\in[0.9,1.3]$; (ii) $\Psi(x)=149$ for all $x\in[0.5,0.8]$; (iii) $\Psi(x)=59{,}875$ for all $x\in[0.3,0.4]$; (iv) $\Psi(0.2)=442{,}414$; and (v) $\Psi(0.1)=24{,}154{,}953$. These values refine the known piecewise-constant behavior of the threshold function and provide explicit numerical information about continuous Bonse-type inequalities; the source does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

title: The Galois group conjecture for the polynomial Q_n
source_name: Karl Dilcher and Maciej Ulas, “Arithmetic properties of polynomial solutions of the Diophantine equation P(x)x^n+1+Q(x)(x+1)^n+1=1”, arXiv:1909.11222 (2019).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (1994–2019). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1909.03541](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.03541), [arXiv:math/9411238](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/9411238).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.11222

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2019).
statement:
Let $n\geq 2$, let $Q_n$ be the polynomial studied in the paper, and write

$$
D_{0,n}=\operatorname{Disc}(Q_n).
$$

For a polynomial with rational coefficients, let $\operatorname{Gal}(Q_n)$ denote its Galois group and let $A_n$ and $S_n$ be the alternating and symmetric groups, respectively. **Galois group conjecture.** For integers $n\geq 2$,

$$
\operatorname{Gal}(Q_n)=\begin{cases}
A_n & \text{if $D_{0,n}$ is a square};\\
S_n & \text{if $D_{0,n}$ is not a square}.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture refines the general fact that a square discriminant forces the Galois group to be contained in an alternating group. It is supported by computations, but no resolution is given here.

title: Louboutin's polynomial identity conjecture for S and R
source_name: Jinwoo Choi and Dohyeong Kim, “On a weak form of Ennola's conjecture about certain cubic number fields”, arXiv:2410.21158 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.21158

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2024). “This is still an open problem. Ennola conjectured in that $\{ \epsilon_l, \epsilon_l-1 \}$ above is a pair of fundamental units for the maximal order $\mathcal{O}$ of $\mathbb{Q}(\epsilon_l)$.”
statement:
For $d\geq 1$, define

$$
P_d(X,Y)=d\sum_{\substack{k,l\geq 0\\0\leq 2k+3l\leq d}}(-1)^{k-1}\binom{k+l}{k}\binom{d-k-2l}{k+l}\frac{X^kY^{d-2k-3l}}{d-k-2l}.
$$

Let $a,b\in\mathbb{Z}$ be nonzero, put $c:=a+b\neq 0$, and define

$$
S_{a,b}(T)=T^{-a}+T^{-b}+T^{a+b}.
$$

For $d\in\{a,b,c\}$,

$$
P_{|d|}(S_{a,b}(T),S_{a,b}(1/T))=-S_{a,b}(1/T^{|d|}).
$$

If $a$ is even and $b$ is odd, also define

$$
R_{a,b}(T)=T^{-a}-(-1)^{a+b}T^{-b}+T^{a+b}.
$$

Then

$$
P_{|d|}(-R_{a,b}(T),-R_{a,b}(1/T))=\begin{cases}-S_{a,b}(1/T^{|d|}),&d=a,\\R_{a,b}(1/T^{|d|}),&d\in\{b,c\}.\end{cases}
$$

This identity is one of Louboutin's conjectures used in the proof of the paper's main theorem; its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

title: The four-cycle conjecture for the abelian loop
source_name: Raghavendra N. Bhat, “An Abelian Loop for Non-Composites”, arXiv:2110.14716 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.14716

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).
statement:
Let $S$ be the abelian loop of odd numbers used in the paper, with binary operation $\bullet$. Consider quartets $(a,b,c,d)$ of distinct numbers in $S$ satisfying

$$
a \bullet b=b \bullet c=c \bullet d=d \bullet a.
$$

**Four-cycle conjecture.** There are infinitely many such quartets.

This conjecture concerns four-cycles in the operation table of the loop. The supplied text does not provide evidence resolving it, so its status remains open.

title: The hafnian analogue of Marcus's inequality for positive semidefinite matrices
source_name: Péter E. Frenkel, “Pfaffians, hafnians and products of real linear functionals”, arXiv:0704.0028 (2008).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0704.0028

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2007).
statement:
Let $p$ be a positive integer and let $A=(a_{i,j})$ be a positive semidefinite symmetric real $n\times n$ matrix. Form the $2pn\times 2pn$ block matrix whose $2p\times 2p$ blocks are all equal to $A$.

**Hafnian inequality.** The hafnian of this block matrix is at least

$$
(2p-1)!!^n\prod_i a_{i,i}^p,
$$

with equality if and only if $A$ has a zero row or is a diagonal matrix.

This is presented as the case $p=1$ obtained from the preceding hafnian inequality together with Marcus's inequality; the general assertion is the proposed extension to arbitrary positive integers $p$.

title: The eigenvalue conjecture for permutation-like matrices
source_name: Steven Robert Lippold, “Permutation-Like Matrices”, arXiv:2403.02478 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02478

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2024). “One open question follows since the polytope (Birkoff Polytope) formed by Doubly Stochastic Matrices is the intersection of the polytopes formed by Left and Right Stochastic Matrices.”
statement:
Let $PL_d$ denote the set of permutation-like matrices of degree $d$, and let $A\in PL_d$ be a permutation-like matrix with $d>1$. A **permutation-like matrix eigenvalue conjecture.** The eigenvalues of $A$ are zero or roots of unity. Further, zero is an eigenvalue if and only if $A$ is neither a permutation matrix nor the identity matrix.

This conjecture proposes that permutation-like matrices retain the root-of-unity spectral behavior of permutation matrices, apart from possible zero eigenvalues. The supplied context reports this as an open conjecture, based on the cases $d=2$ and $d=3$.

title: The determinant and inverse conjecture for E0_2-matrices
source_name: Bharat Pratap Chauhan and Dipti Dubey, “On semimonotone matrices of exact order two”, arXiv:2603.00639 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00639

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2026).
statement:
Let $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ be an $\mathbf{E_{0_2}}$-matrix.

**Determinant and inverse conjecture.** One has

$$
\det(A)<0,
$$

$A^{-1}$ exists, and $A^{-1}$ is a $\mathbf{Z}$-matrix.

This is one of the conjectures proposed after examples and observations about $\mathbf{E_{0_2}}$-matrices. The supplied text gives no evidence of a proof or refutation, so its resolution remains open.

title: Primitive powers conjecture for integer matrices
source_name: Nir Ailon and Zeev Rudnick, “Torsion points on curves and common divisors of a^k-1 and b^k-1”, arXiv:math/0202102 (2002).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0202102

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2002).
statement: Let $r\geq 2$ and let $A\in \operatorname{Mat}_r(\mathbf Z)$ be nonsingular. Define $\gcd(A-I)$ as the greatest common divisor of the entries of $A-I$, and call $A$ **primitive** when $\gcd(A-I)=1$. Assume that $A$ has a pair of multiplicatively independent eigenvalues. **Primitive powers conjecture.** The matrix $A^k$ is primitive for infinitely many positive integers $k$. This conjecture proposes that, provided the matrix is initially primitive and has sufficient multiplicative independence among its eigenvalues, its powers return to the primitive condition infinitely often. The paper presents this as an analogue of the scalar conjecture for common divisors; its resolution is not given in the source.

title: Johnson's determinantal identity for contiguous minors of Toeplitz matrices
source_name: Teng Zhang, “Johnson's determinantal identity for contiguous minors of Toeplitz matrices, with an accretive extension”, arXiv:2601.18977 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18977

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2026).
statement:
Let $M_n(\mathbb{R})$ denote the real $n\times n$ matrices. For $A\in M_n(\mathbb{R})$, write $A_r(i,j)$ for the $r\times r$ contiguous submatrix beginning at row $i$ and column $j$. A matrix is **Toeplitz** if its entries are constant along diagonals, and let $J_n$ be the $n\times n$ matrix whose entries are all $1$.

**Johnson's conjecture.** For every $n\ge 2$ and every Toeplitz matrix $A\in M_n(\mathbb{R})$ satisfying $A+A^{\top}=2J_n$,

$$
\ndet A_{n-1}(1,2)+det A_{n-1}(2,1)=2det A_{n-1}(1,1).
$$

The identity is a determinantal relation among contiguous minors, motivated by Dodgson's condensation formula. The supplied source does not state whether Johnson's conjecture has been resolved.

title: Lin–van den Driessche conjecture on Schatten norm compression
source_name: arXiv
references: - [Three-Point Trace Positivity:Schatten Norm Compression and Interpolating Metrics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11021) — arXiv — Trung Dung Vuong, Hiroyuki Osaka
progress_summary:
The conjecture concerns whether replacing blocks of a partitioned $2\times N$ matrix by their Schatten $p$-norms decreases the resulting norm for $1\le p\le2$. The retrieved literature records partial results but does not establish the full statement.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/html/math/0702186v2)*

**Known results**

- The conjectured inequality is reported for several special cases, including Hanner’s matrix inequality as a special case.
- For $3\times3$ and larger block partitions, examples show that the proposed inequality can fail.
- Some special cases extend to $0\le p\le1$, but this extension is not valid in general.



Current status (as of October 2026): The general Schatten c
statement: For every integer $N\ge 1$, every finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces $E_1,\ldots,E_N,F_1,F_2$, every block operator $A=[A_{ij}]_{i=1,j=1}^{2,N}$ with $A_{ij}:E_j\to F_i$, and every $1\le p\le 2$, one has $\left\|[\|A_{ij}\|_{S_p}]_{i=1,j=1}^{2,N}\right\|_{S_p}\le \left\|[A_{ij}]_{i=1,j=1}^{2,N}\right\|_{S_p}$, where the matrix on the left is the scalar $2\times N$ matrix of block Schatten $p$-norms.

title: Norm-one conjecture for dominant eigenvectors of non-negative premagic matrices
source_name: Kardi Teknomo, “Premagic and Ideal Flow Matrices”, arXiv:1706.08856 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.08856

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).
statement: Let $\mathbf{M}$ be a non-negative premagic matrix, and let $\mathbf{v}$ be an eigenvector corresponding to its dominant eigenvalue. **Norm-one conjecture.** Both the $2$-norm and the Frobenius norm of $\mathbf{v}$ are equal to one. This is presented as a computational conjecture about eigenvectors of non-negative premagic matrices; a mathematical proof is not supplied.

title: Gupta–Rai conjecture on permutation trinomials over finite fields
source_name: Daniele Bartoli, Mohit Pal and Pantelimon Stanica, “A proof of a conjecture on permutation trinomials”, arXiv:2410.22692 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.22692

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).
statement:
Let $q=p^k$, where $p>7$ is a prime and $k>1$, and let $ff$ be the finite field with $q$ elements. For $alpha\inff^*$, define

$$
f(X)=X^{q(p-1)+1}+\alpha X^{pq}+X^{q+p-1}.
$$

**Gupta–Rai conjecture.** The trinomial $f(X)$ is a permutation polynomial over $\mathbb F_{q^2}$ if and only if $\alpha=-1$ and $k=2$.
This conjecture concerns the permutation behaviour of a family of trinomials over quadratic extensions of finite fields. Earlier work establishes related classifications in characteristics $3$, $5$, and $7$, while the case $p>7$ and $k>1$ is the proposed general case.

title: Circulant unistochastic matrices and circulant unitary matrices conjecture
source_name: Grzegorz Rajchel-Mieldzioć, Kamil Korzekwa, Zbigniew Puchała and Karol Życzkowski, “Algebraic and geometric structures inside the Birkhoff polytope”, arXiv:2101.11288 (2021).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.11288

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).
statement: Let $\mathcal{C}_d$ denote the set of circulant matrices, $\mathcal{U}_d$ the set of unistochastic matrices, and $\mathcal{C}_d^2$ the set of doubly circulant unistochastic matrices. The paper establishes that $\mathcal{C}_d\cap\mathcal{U}_d=\mathcal{C}_d^2$ for dimensions $d\leq 4$. **Circulant unistochastic matrices conjecture.** The sets $\mathcal{C}_d\cap\mathcal{U}_d$ and $\mathcal{C}_d^2$ coincide for all $d$; equivalently, every circulant unistochastic matrix has a corresponding circulant unitary matrix. This extends the result proved in dimensions at most four and remains open in general.

title: Conjecture on the eigenvalue multiplicities of the Stern recurrence matrices
source_name: Richard P. Stanley, “Some Linear Recurrences Motivated by Stern's Diatomic Array”, arXiv:1901.04647 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.04647

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).
statement:
For each positive integer $r$, let $A_r$ be the matrix governing the recurrence for $u_r(n)$. Write $[a_0,\dots,a_{q-1}]_q$ for the periodic function $f\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying $f(n)=a_i$ when $n\equiv i\pmod q$, and let $e_r(\theta)$ denote the number of eigenvalues of $A_r$ equal to $\theta$. An eigenvalue is **semisimple** when the minimum polynomial is not divisible by $(x-\theta)^2$, equivalently when all its Jordan blocks have size one.

**Eigenvalue multiplicity conjecture.** For positive integers $s$, the following hold:

(a) 

$$
e_{2s-1}(0)=\frac{1}{3}s+[0,-\frac{1}{3},\frac{1}{3}]_3.
$$

The eigenvalue $0$ is semisimple; there are no other multiple eigenvalues, and $1$ is not an eigenvalue.

(b)

$$
e_{2s}(1)=\frac{1}{6}s+[-1,-\frac{1}{6},-\frac{1}{3},-\frac{1}{2},-\frac{2}{3},\frac{1}{6}]_6,
$$

$$
e_{2s}(-1)=e_{2s+6}(1).
$$

The eigenvalues $1$ and $-1$ are semisimple, and there are no other multiple eigenvalues.

These assertions would sharpen the naive recurrence-order bounds by identifying repeated eigenvalues and their Jordan structure. They are presented as conjectures based on the paper's computations; no proof or resolution is supplied.

title: The anti-regular graph conjecture on extremal eigenvalues of threshold graphs
source_name: Fernando Tura, “A conjecture of eigenvalues of threshold graphs”, arXiv:2006.03136 (2020).
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2018–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1908.03954](https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.03954), [arXiv:1807.07591](https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.07591).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.03136

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).
statement: A **threshold graph** is a graph obtained from an isolated vertex by repeatedly adding either an isolated vertex or a dominating vertex. Let $A_n$ denote the anti-regular graph on $n$ vertices, namely the threshold graph with only two vertices of equal degree. **Anti-regular graph conjecture.** For each $n$, among all threshold graphs on $n$ vertices, $A_n$ has the smallest positive eigenvalue and the largest negative eigenvalue less than $-1$. This conjecture concerns the extremal nontrivial eigenvalues of threshold graphs. Earlier work established partial results and identified critical cases requiring a more refined method; the conjecture is presented here as the problem addressed by the paper.

title: The order divisibility conjecture for (anti)palindromic graphs
source_name: Tadashi Akagi and Eduardo A. Canale, “The Palindromic Trees”, arXiv:2212.02957 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.02957

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2022).
statement: Let a graph be **(anti)palindromic** if it has the palindromic or antipalindromic symmetry defined in the paper, and let its order be its number of vertices. **Order divisibility conjecture.** Every (anti)palindromic graph has order multiple of four (plus two). By the preceding corollary, the claim is proved for (anti)palindromic trees; the authors report computer searches suggesting that it holds for any graph, but no general proof is given.

title: Conjecture on the Laplacian eigenvalue distribution of graphs with given diameter
source_name: Leyou Xu and Bo Zhou, “Diameter vs Laplacian eigenvalue distribution”, arXiv:2401.03777 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.03777

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$ with diameter $d\ge 2$. For an interval of indices, write $m_G[a,b]$ for the number of Laplacian eigenvalues of $G$ whose indices lie between $a$ and $b$, inclusive.

**Laplacian eigenvalue distribution conjecture.** If $c=0,\dots,d-2$ and

$$
\max\{2,c\}\le d\le n-2-c,
$$

then

$$
m_G[n-d+2-c,n]\le n-d+c.
$$

The conjecture concerns how many of the largest Laplacian eigenvalues a connected graph of diameter $d$ can have in the indicated index range. The source states that it is known for $c=0,1,2,d-3,d-2$, while the general case remains open.
